transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-09
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 58 minutes (approx)
Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Maya (Redwood SE), Derek (Redwood CSM); Dr. Lena Ortiz, Amit Rao, Priya Singh, Marco Fuentes (CytoForm)

Summary: preliminary security & compliance review focused on SAML/SCIM provisioning patterns, least-privilege RBAC mapping, audit log retention and KMS key ownership options for a Private deployment - customer evaluating Redwood Private vs Dedicated for regulated workloads.

Topics: SOC 2 / ISO status, SAML IdP metadata & assertion mapping, SCIM attribute sync cadence, role hierarchy and least-privilege patterns, audit log format/retention, encryption/KMS and HSM options, data residency implications for on-prem vs cloud region, rollout plan for pilot.

--- Transcript ---
[00:00] Jordan (Redwood): hey everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate you squeezing this in. uh, quick roll call?
[00:08] Dr. Lena Ortiz (CytoForm): yep, lena here, hi.
[00:10] Amit Rao (CytoForm): Amit on from infra.
[00:12] Priya Singh (CytoForm): Priya, platform.
[00:14] Marco Fuentes (CytoForm): Marco, compliance.
[00:16] Maya (Redwood): Maya Chen, platform SE at Redwood.
[00:18] Derek (Redwood): Derek, CSM, quick intro.
[00:20] Jordan (Redwood): cool, agenda - we want to walk SAML/SCIM mapping, show RBAC patterns for least privilege, and talk through audit logs and KMS ownership options. save time for questions and next steps. sound good?
[00:32] Dr. Lena Ortiz: yes, that's perfect. we are under a hard compliance window - ISO in Q3 and SOC2 evidence needed sooner, so need very clear controls and how logs are retained.
[00:44] Jordan: understood, we'll call out retention windows and evidence surfaces. quick question on deployment: are you leaning Private (on-prem/vpc) or Dedicated?
[00:53] Amit: leaning Private since patient-data-adjacent. some workloads might live in our cloud region but core inference must be in our VPC.
[01:03] Maya: ok good we support both, and for Private you can choose customer-managed KMS or Redwood-managed depending on your compliance posture. note, customer-managed KMS requires key escrow policies and we can integrate with common HSMs.
[01:19] Marco: on KMS - can you support Bring Your Own Key and HSM? requirement from our auditors.
[01:26] Maya: yes, BYOK is supported for Private and Dedicated with HSM-backed keys. there's a small integration step to register the key ARN and configure rotation policies. we also have an option to keep logs segregated per-tenant.
[01:38] Priya: how are audit logs exposed? we need syslog export and immutable storage for 1 year.
[01:45] Derek: we can stream logs to your SIEM via SIEM connector, also provide an append-only audit log export (S3 or on-prem object store). retention policy's configurable; default is 90 days for hosted, but Private can be set to 365+ per contract.
[01:59] Dr. Lena Ortiz: good. also need to know what the audit events look like - admin actions, API key issues, model rollout changes, and RBAC grants.
[02:08] Maya: we'll share sample event schema; events include actor, action, resource, old/new state, timestamp, and request context. tiny caveat: some model inference traces may be redacted by default for privacy.
[02:21] Jordan: quick dive into SAML/SCIM - Maya will walk through an example flow.
[02:28] Maya: sure. so SAML is the auth flow - IdP issues assertions, we map assertion attributes to user identity. SCIM is provisioning/sync - typically we do group-to-role mapping so groups in your IdP map to Redwood roles. common mapping is e.g., 'cytoform-admins' -> admin role, 'platform-eng' -> infra role.
[02:47] Priya: what attributes do you need in the SAML assertion?
[02:50] Maya: core ones: NameID (prefer email), email, given_name, family_name. for SCIM we recommend externalId, userName, and groups. we'll send you a template.
[03:03] Amit: we do automatic deprovisioning via SCIM on delete - does Redwood honor immediate deprovision or is there a grace window?
[03:11] Maya: by default we honor immediate deprovision, but can configure a grace window (e.g., 24-72 hrs) if you want soft-delete behavior. note: immediate removal will invalidate tokens and drop active sessions.
[03:24] Marco: auditors will ask about orphaned keys and service accounts - what's the recommended least-privilege model?
[03:30] Maya: recommend role-scoped service accounts, with narrowly-scoped roles for ingestion vs model management. avoid using account owner for automation. also enable session timeouts and MFA at IdP.
[03:41] Dr. Lena Ortiz: can RBAC be hierarchical? we have nested roles across business units.
[03:46] Jordan: yes, we support role inheritance patterns; our console shows role composition. but for audit clarity we suggest flatter roles and explicit role-to-permission mapping.
[03:56] Priya: what about granular model-level permissions? need to limit who can rollout models to prod.
[04:02] Maya: we support model-level perms: roles can be scoped to models or model groups, and rollouts can be gated by approval workflows. there's an API so you can automate approvals via CI/CD.
[04:13] Amit: does the SCIM group sync allow attribute-based provisioning, like sync only groups with a prefix?
[04:18] Maya: yes, we can filter by group prefix or membership rules. some customers sync all groups but map only a subset into Redwood to keep surface small.
[04:28] Jordan: quick note on SAML metadata: we support both SP-initiated and IdP-initiated flows. you can upload IdP metadata XML or provide metadata URL.
[04:38] Dr. Lena Ortiz: what about certificate rotation? our policy is quarterly rotation for SAML certs.
[04:44] Maya: supported - rolling updates without downtime. we recommend two certs in parallel for zero-downtime swap.
[04:52] Marco: re data residency - if we run Private in our VPC, are logs and models guaranteed to stay in our account?
[04:59] Maya: yes, in Private deployments we can write logs and store artifacts in your object store; model weights can be hosted in your storage or in a customer-owned bucket. for Dedicated there's shared infra so we provide region guarantees and tenant isolation but not customer-owned storage unless in a private offering.
[05:16] Priya: do you encrypt at rest and in transit by default?
[05:19] Maya: TLS in transit, and at-rest encryption via KMS. for Private you can use your KMS keys; for hosted we use Redwood-managed keys unless BYOK is requested.
[05:31] Amit: can we get an architecture diagram for the Private setup? network flows, egress points, and SAML calls to IdP?
[05:38] Jordan: yes, we'll include an architecture sketch in the follow-up doc pack.
[05:42] Dr. Lena Ortiz: auditors also want change history for role grants and who approved them.
[05:47] Derek: every grant action is logged with approver and reason; we also support approval workflows where approvals become part of the record. those logs are exportable for audits.
[05:58] Priya: one more - secrets and env var handling for model deployment, are those stored encrypted and audited?
[06:04] Maya: secrets are stored encrypted via KMS and access to them is logged; we can support per-namespace secret scopes and short-lived tokens to minimize risk.
[06:16] Jordan: ok shifting to the RBAC matrix example - Maya: please walk through a sample mapping.
[06:22] Maya: example: create roles: viewer (read-only, no token creation), developer (can create and test in dev namespaces), deployment-approver (can publish to prod with 2 approvals), admin (full). map IdP groups: 'cyto-dev' -> developer, 'cyto-approvers' -> deployment-approver. also recommend avoiding 'owner' as daily role.
[06:45] Priya: can we write custom predicates, like only allow rollouts during a maintenance window?
[06:50] Maya: yes policy engine supports time-based conditions and IP allow-lists - those are enforced at policy evaluation time.
[06:58] Amit: for the pilot, do you support token scoping so we can run ephemeral test services?
[07:03] Maya: yes short-lived tokens are supported and recommended for automation; they can be minted via API or via our CI/CD integration.
[07:12] Dr. Lena Ortiz: on SCIM, how do you handle attribute mismatch and user merging? we have users with multiple emails.
[07:20] Maya: we match on externalId or primary email, and provide a reconciliation UI; merges are manual by default to avoid accidental merges, but can be automated with strict rules.
[07:33] Marco: auditors worry about admin access sprawl - how do you detect unused privileges?
[07:38] Derek: we have an access review export and an entitlement report - run monthly to identify stale accounts and roles that haven't been used. we can also integrate with your IAM governance tools.
[07:50] Jordan: quick note about vulnerabilities: we provide patch windows and CVE notifications for the runtime; Private can be scheduled for your maintenance windows.
[07:59] Priya: what about network egress - does Redwood call home for telemetry?
[08:05] Maya: minimal telemetry for health metrics; in Private telemetry can be disabled and logs sent only to your endpoints. for hosted, basic telemetry is on but can be limited.
[08:15] Amit: let's talk about timeline - we need SOC2 evidence in 6 weeks for the procurement packet. can you provide that?
[08:22] Jordan: yes we'll share SOC2 Type II report and control matrix; it'll have redactions but enough for procurement.
[08:28] Dr. Lena Ortiz: will that suffice for auditors or do we need an onsite walkthrough?
[08:33] Marco: sometimes auditors ask for a live demo of controls.
[08:36] Derek: we can do an auditor walkthrough - typically a 60-90 min session with our security lead, we can schedule that if needed.
[08:46] Priya: for the pilot, can we start with a non-prod Private deployment in our VPC? we want to test SCIM sync and audit exports.
[08:55] Maya: absolutely - pilot in your VPC is standard. we'll provide terraform modules and a runbook.
[09:02] Jordan: ok next I'll recap action items. but first questions?
[09:06] Amit: do you have an SLO for latency? not strictly security but relevant for model guard rails.
[09:12] Maya: SLOs vary by config; Dedicated provides 99th percentile latency targets; Private is dependent on your infra but we publish profiling guides. for pilot we'll run a small benchmark.
[09:24] Dr. Lena Ortiz: one more - is there support for data residency in EU region for any cross-border concerns?
[09:30] Maya: yes we have region pinning and can ensure data at rest is kept in EU for EU-tenants. for Private that's simpler since it's in your VPC.
[09:39] Jordan: recap - Jordan will send SOC2 and ISO cert links; Maya will send SCIM/SAML templates, sample audit event schema, and an architecture sketch; Priya will share role lists for RBAC mapping; we'll schedule pilot kickoff w/infra.
[09:54] Dr. Lena Ortiz: thanks - can we get a redacted SOC2 by Friday?
[09:58] Jordan: we'll aim for Friday, if not early next week.
[10:02] Marco: good. any blockers?
[10:05] Maya: the only blocker is network peering approvals on your side for Private. once that's cleared we can deploy the pilot.
[10:12] Priya: noted, we'll start approvals.
[10:16] Jordan: ok I'll wrap. thanks all. we'll follow up with doc pack and calendar invites.
[10:22] Dr. Lena Ortiz: thanks everyone.
[10:24] meeting end.

Notes on transcription: some words may be misheard, eg "precedence" or product names. references to KV cache occasionally mocked as "KV cash" in some mentions, please refer to official docs in the follow-up pack.
